lemma: Upper bound for the blow-up basis. For a graph G=(V,E), n=|V|, m=|E|, let K_G be the GF(3) kernel with vertex blocks in T_3={t: sum t=0} and edge coordinates forced by k(e,c)=-(k(u,c)+k(w,c)); dim K_G = 2n. Let B = {x_v, x'_v : v in V} with x_v=(1,2,0), x'_v=(0,1,2) in the vertex-v block (zero elsewhere) and edge coordinates forced as above. Then (i) B is a basis of K_G; (ii) H_B (support-intersection graph) is G[K_2], the lexicographic product with K_2; (iii) tw(G[K_2]) <= 2 tw(G)+1; hence min over bases of tw(H_B) <= 2 tw(G)+1 (tightness of the upper side, for this explicit B).

proved_step: PROOF. (i) The projection K_G -> (+)_v T_3 onto vertex blocks is an isomorphism (edge coordinates are determined by endpoints), so dim K_G = 2n. The vectors (1,2,0) and (0,1,2) lie in T_3 (sums 3 = 0) and are linearly independent over GF(3), so their vertex-block images for all v form a basis of (+)_v T_3. Hence B is a basis of K_G. (ii) Vertices of H_B are the 2n vectors. Same-vertex pair x_v, x'_v: they share vertex-block coordinates 1 and 2 (supports {0,1} and {1,2}), so they are adjacent. Pair with u != v: vertex blocks are disjoint, so a shared coordinate must be an edge coordinate e; the coordinate of x_v on e is nonzero only if e is incident to v. A shared edge e must therefore be incident to both u and v, i.e. e=(u,v) in E. For such an edge, supports of x_u and x_v on e are {0,1} and {1,2}-type sets that overlap (both contain coordinate 1 when the pair uses (1,2,0) and (0,1,2); for the other combinations the supports {0,1},{0,1} and {1,2},{1,2} also overlap), so all four pairs between blobs of adjacent u,v are adjacent. Non-adjacent u,v have no shared coordinate. So H_B = G[K_2]. (iii) Let (T,{X_i}) be a tree decomposition of G of width k. Replace each bag X_i by X_i x {a,b} (2 copies). Bag size is at most 2(k+1), so width <= 2k+1. Coverage: a vertex pair (v,a),(v,b) lies in the bag of any bag containing v. An edge (u,a)-(w,b) of G[K_2] comes from edge uw in G, which lies in some X_i, so both appear in X_i x {a,b}. Connectivity of the occurrence sets is inherited from T. Hence tw(G[K_2]) <= 2k+1. The reverse inequality (min over ALL bases >= 2tw(G)+1) is NOT proved here; it is the owner's lower bound and is not re-verified in this step. Remark: this explains the earlier hill-climb stall for P3 and C4: the explicit B reaches tw 3 (P3) and tw 5 (C4), which the search had not found.
